clue.text: Not required to show/ forbearance

definitions.meaning: to show mercy, to refrain from punishing someone

explanation.walkthrough: The slash in the clue is a mark from the printed page and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surplus to needs is extra, and to let someone off out of mercy is to refrain from harming them.

clue.text: Tidal flow that can ruin a sweater

indicators.note: ruin tells us the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that the incoming tide could spoil a woollen jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can ruin' rearranges A SWEATER into the answer; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide is a movement of the ocean's salty liquid.

clue.text: Stops sleeping

parts.note: read as someone coming out of slumber, not as a person who halts while asleep

explanation.definitionFit: Ceasing to slumber is rousing oneself, rising from rest.

clue.text: Part of the borough of York

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a stretch of letters inside the following words

explanation.surface: A remark about a district within the city of York.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'thE BORough'. Ebor is the old Latin-derived abbreviation for York, seen in the Archbishop of York's signature and the Ebor horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebor is the short form of Eboracum, the Roman name for the city, still used for it.

clue.text: Said and done in the form of a complaint

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are reshaped into another form, a signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Something that has been spoken and carried out as a formal grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the form of' rearranges SAID and DONE; 'and' is a link. The complaint is medical, swollen tissue at the back of the nose, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a complaint, and swollen tissue behind the nose is a common childhood one.

clue.text: What made the union go to pieces?

definitions.text: What made the union go to pieces?

parts.words: What made the union go to pieces?
parts.note: a union going to pieces is falling apart, the opposite of being made whole, read as a marriage or alliance collapsing

explanation.definitionFit: Breaking up into fragments is a crumbling, the undoing of unity.

clue.text: Things cracked up to cause bewilderment?

definitions.text: Things cracked up to cause bewilderment?

parts.words: Things cracked up to cause bewilderment?
parts.note: things cracked are hard-shelled kernels opened with crackers; cracked up also means gone mad, and the word means crazy

explanation.definitionFit: Hazels and walnuts are cracked open, and the same word is slang for insane or bewildered.

clue.text: I call round on pressing business

indicators.note: round says the word for call goes around the following word

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone says they will phone about some urgent matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pressing business' is pressing clothes with a hot iron, not urgent work; 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing creases out of clothes with a hot appliance is a household chore.

clue.text: A Scot on the line from Bedford to Cambridge

definitions.meaning: a stock Scottish man's name, short for Alexander

definitions.text: on the line from Bedford to Cambridge
definitions.meaning: a small town in Bedfordshire, England, lying between those two places

explanation.surface: A Scotsman travelling on an English railway route.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy is a market town in Bedfordshire, an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy is a familiar Scottish nickname for Alexander, and Sandy is a Bedfordshire town between Bedford and Cambridge.

clue.text: The last things toddlers want to be told by their nannies

definitions.text: The last things toddlers want to be told by their nannies

parts.words: The last things toddlers want to be told by their nannies
parts.note: read as what small children least wish to hear, but in fact the tales told last thing at night

explanation.definitionFit: Tales read to children before sleep are the final things they are told each day.

clue.text: Fashionable kind of light glossy silk

definitions.meaning: in style, from the French phrase meaning in the fashion
a thin lustrous silk once used for hoods and scarves

explanation.surface: A trendy sort of shiny fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in the current style, and the same word names a thin shiny silk fabric.

clue.text: Plight of Wimbledon struggler put in writing?

definitions.meaning: a player who is a set behind in a tennis match

explanation.surface: The difficulties of a tennis player at Wimbledon, recorded in print.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London grass-court tennis championship; a match there is won in sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player losing at Wimbledon is behind by a set, and to record something on paper is to note it.

clue.text: Said to draw attention to a border

parts.note: a hem is the folded edge or border of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone points out an edge or margin.
explanation.walkthrough: The cough-like word people say to get noticed is built from A and a word for a border; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A little throat-clearing noise is uttered to get people to notice the speaker.

clue.text: All agreed to make amends?

explanation.surface: A whole group consents to put things right.
explanation.definitionFit: When everyone is in harmony they are united, and to make up for a wrong is to expiate it.

clue.text: A bloomer that is purely symbolic

definitions.text: A bloomer that is purely symbolic

parts.words: A bloomer that is purely symbolic
parts.note: a bloomer is a flower, here one that stands as an emblem of purity

explanation.definitionFit: This white flower is a traditional emblem of purity and innocence.

clue.text: Net result of the game

parts.note: the final tally of points or goals, net suggesting the goal net

explanation.definitionFit: The final tally of goals or points is what a match ends with.

clue.text: A custom that makes us mature

parts.note: to age is to mature, grow older

explanation.surface: A tradition that helps us grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that makes' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual practice or convention is an established way of doing things.

clue.text: Doubly facile philosophy of the spendthrift who has come into a fortune

definitions.text: Doubly facile philosophy of the spendthrift who has come into a fortune

parts.words: Doubly facile philosophy of the spendthrift who has come into a fortune
parts.note: the saying uses the word for facile twice, and describes money that arrives freely and is spent just as freely

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says what was gained without effort is lost without regret, the outlook of a careless heir.

clue.text: It was reviewed before, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking again, a hint to re-view the letters in a new order

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Something was examined earlier, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' looks like 'looked over again' but is the anagram signal; the phrase hedges a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase hedges a statement, meaning so to speak or seemingly.

clue.text: Put one's sorrow into words

parts.note: to voice one's apology or sadness, the polite phrase used when declining or apologising

explanation.definitionFit: To voice an apology or sadness aloud is to say you are sorry.

clue.text: Inquisitorial Spaniard seen to mix freely

indicators.note: freely says the letters move about without restraint into a new order

explanation.surface: A Spanish inquisitor is spotted mingling with people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges SEEN and MIX; 'to' is a link. Cardinal Ximenes was a Grand Inquisitor of Spain, and the pseudonym of a famous Observer crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Jiménez de Cisneros led the Spanish Inquisition in the early sixteenth century.

clue.text: A gourmet taking mince pie with a French parish priest

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the letters are chopped and reordered

parts.note: a curé is a parish priest in France

explanation.surface: A food lover eats a mince pie in the company of a French vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of 'mince pie' but tells you to scramble PIE into EPI; 'taking' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of fine food and drink is someone devoted to refined eating.

clue.text: A goblin being taught to make painful progress?

parts.note: L stands for learner, someone being taught, as on a learner driver's plate
an imp is a small mischievous goblin

explanation.surface: A little sprite struggling through its lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate, so L means someone being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble is to walk with difficulty because of an injury.

clue.text: Nominally it goes on record

parts.note: a name tag goes on things in name only, and a record company's name goes on a disc

explanation.definitionFit: A tag carries a name, and a record company's brand is printed on its discs.

clue.text: Sacks brought round to sit on, maybe

indicators.note: brought round says the word is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a stool is something to sit on, the maybe marking an example

explanation.surface: Bags carried over to be used as seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' turns STOOL backwards. 'Sacks' is a verb here, to plunder, not bags.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to pillage and plunder it.

clue.text: When corruption is about I show no respect for authority

indicators.note: is about says the word for corruption surrounds the following letter

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Someone says they defy authority whenever corruption is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts I inside ROT; 'When' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage in public disorder is to rebel violently against those in charge.

clue.text: Was page saying what stung him?

parts.note: taken as written; that its letters plus the P of page also run across 'Was page' is a coincidence, as page is the abbreviation P

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the page boy caused the sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped insect with a sting in its tail is what delivers a painful sting.

clue.text: One who makes sure he doesn't waste a thing

definitions.text: One who makes sure he doesn't waste a thing

indicators.note: makes signals that the next word is made into something new by reordering its letters

explanation.surface: A thrifty person who is careful never to squander anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges SURE; the whole clue also describes someone who puts things to use rather than wasting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts things to use rather than throwing them away employs every item.

clue.text: Sub-continental citizen of Belgian extraction

indicators.note: extraction suggests letters pulled out and put back in another order

explanation.surface: An Indian national who is of Belgian descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraction' reads as ancestry but rearranges BELGIAN; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Bengal, in India or Bangladesh, is a native of the subcontinent.

clue.text: Humble science graduate cutting round a Yorkshire river

indicators.note: cutting says the graduate cuts into the other letters

parts.note: O is round in shape
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire
BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

explanation.surface: A modest scientist cutting a path round a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Ure flows through North Yorkshire, England; 'cutting' is the container signal, the degree cutting into the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowly or of little renown describes a person without fame or rank.

clue.text: Clarion call for retreat

parts.note: a bugle signal sounded at dusk in the army, and at military funerals

explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call played at nightfall in British forces signals the end of the day, and is sounded at remembrance services.

clue.text: Pilgrim who told a racy yarn about an errant wife

definitions.text: Pilgrim who told a racy yarn about an errant wife

parts.words: Pilgrim who told a racy yarn about an errant wife
parts.note: one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims, whose bawdy tale concerns a miller's wife and daughter

explanation.walkthrough: The Canterbury Tales, by Geoffrey Chaucer, has pilgrims each telling a story; the steward's tale is ribald.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales the estate steward tells a bawdy story about a cuckolded miller.
